nodes.title: Your Privacy Choices
nodes.body:
As described in our Privacy Policy, we collect personal information from your interactions with us and our website, including through cookies and similar technologies. We may also share this personal information with third parties, including advertising partners. We do this in order to show you ads on other websites that are more relevant to your interests and for other reasons outlined in our privacy policy.

Sharing of personal information for targeted advertising based on your interaction on different websites may be considered "sales", "sharing", or "targeted advertising" under certain U.S. state privacy laws. Depending on where you live, you may have the right to opt out of these activities. If you would like to exercise this opt-out right, please follow the instructions below.

If you visit our website with the Global Privacy Control opt-out preference signal enabled, depending on where you are, we will treat this as a request to opt-out of activity that may be considered a “sale” or “sharing” of personal information or other uses that may be considered targeted advertising for the device and browser you used to visit our website.

nodes.title: 12 in. LapMaster Manual
nodes.body:
Welcome to your new Rhino Lapidary 12” LapMaster!

  • Flat Lap Tapered Bolt

  • Flat Lap 1” Washer

  • Flat Lap 1 ½” Washer

INITIAL SETUP

Note: The following is not included but required for use: a water source for dripping onto the flat lap, a container for wastewater, and 12” grinding plates. Both regular and magnetic 12” grinding laps can be attached to this machine.

Magnetic grinding laps adhere nicely to the metal rotation table. Screw-on grinding laps can be attached by removing the tapered bolt, inserting the 1” washer, placing the lap onto the rotation table, then placing the 1 ½” washer in its center. Then insert the bolt through the washers and flat lap, tightening them to the rotation table.

Note: You may need to halt the rotational movement of the flat lap table to begin tightening any components. This can be done using the ROTATIONAL LOCK (detailed below).

GENERAL

The 12” LapMaster is 19” in width and 25” in depth, and weighs approximately 90lbs. The machine frame is made of 6mm-thick reinforced steel.

Power Control Box:

The power control box is mounted on the back of the machine, and has three visible controls. The green cylindrical indicator light on the front of the control box turns on when power is supplied to the machine. The red speed dial on the front of the control box can be turned between on and off to start the flat lap. There is a red and yellow emergency stop button on the top of the control box. To stop the machine during operation, press the emergency stop button. Once the emergency stop has been engaged, it needs to be disengaged before operation can resume, which is done by twisting the emergency stop button clockwise.

Motor and Electrical Requirements:

The LapMaster’s 1 Horsepower motor runs on 110 Volts and it is highly recommended to operate this motor on a minimum 20 amperage circuit.

Important: Do not run this machine on a circuit or voltage not recommended for this machine. Motor start-up can jump to 21-22 amperage but will then settle back to below 20 amps. Make sure the machine has its own circuit for best performance.

The default LapMaster motor runs at 1400rpm. On the Rhino Lapidary website, you may request a LapMaster with a variable speed motor, which can run between 500rpm and 1500rpm. 

LAP ROTATION TABLE

Note: You may need to halt the rotational movement of the flat lap table to begin tightening any components. This can be done using the ROTATIONAL LOCK (detailed below).

The lap rotation table is located on the top of the machine. It consists of two parts: the outer lap base and the center bolt. The center bolt is secured onto a left-handed thread bolt, so tightening it must be done in the counterclockwise direction. The outer lap base is tightened normally by spinning clockwise.

Important: Do NOT operate this machine without first setting up a water drip for your flat lap. Running the machine while dry will damage both the flat lap and the rocks being processed.

ROTATIONAL LOCK

You may need to halt the rotational movement of the flat lap table to begin tightening any components. The rotational lock is a metal push-pin with a black knob handle located on the lower left side of the machine. To engage the rotational lock, push the pin inwards. This will rotationally lock the lap rotation table.

WATER DRAIN

The LapMaster’s water drain is located on the bottom of the machine. This drain is not closable and should be piped to a separate reservoir for operation. Do not pour your wastewater slurry down the drain, as the sediment can harden within your pipes. Let the sediment settle to the bottom of your containers. You may pour out the container on a gravel area, or you may let the water evaporate and dispose of the sludge in the trash or a gravel area.

Important: Rhino Lapidary suggests connecting the machine to a reservoir by attaching rubber tubing to the drain using either a gasket or a ziptie.

Welcome to your new Rhino Lapidary 18” LapMaster!

The water spout must be hooked up to a continuous water source, and can then be used by turning the blue valve to initiate or cease the water drip.

Important: DO NOT operate the LapMaster dry. Operation must always be paired with a water drip for the safety of the machine and proper treatment of your specimens.

GENERAL

The 18” LapMaster is XX” in width and XX” in depth, and weighs approximately XXlbs. The machine frame is made of 6mm-thick reinforced steel.

Power Control Box:
The power control box is mounted on the back of the machine, and has five(?) visible controls: 

  1. The red cylindrical indicator light at the top right corner of the control box turns on when the machine is powered on. 

  2. The green cylindrical indicator light to the left of the power indicator light turns on when the machine is in operation.

  3. There is a red and yellow emergency stop button below the two indicator lights. To stop the machine during operation, press the emergency stop button. Once the emergency stop has been engaged, it needs to be disengaged before operation can resume, which is done by twisting the emergency stop button clockwise.

  5. The black speed dial below the emergency stop button can be turned to adjust the flat lap’s revolutions per minute while the machine is operating. 

  6. The red switch at the bottom of the control box supplies power to the machine. Turning the switch counterclockwise turns the power off.

The LapMaster’s 1 Horsepower motor runs on 110 Volts and it is highly recommended to operate this motor on a minimum 20 amperage circuit.

The 18” LapMaster motor is a variable speed motor, which can run between 500rpm and 1500rpm. Slower speeds are desirable for fine grits, polishing, and softer stones, while faster speeds are desirable for coarser grits and harder stones.

This will rotationally lock the lap rotation table.

Grinding Discs:
The LapMaster does not come with flat lap grinding attachments. Both regular and magnetic 18” grinding laps can be attached to this machine. Ensure all surfaces are thoroughly clean when switching discs to a different grit. 

Magnetic grinding laps adhere nicely to the metal rotation table. Screw-on grinding laps can be attached by removing the tapered bolt, inserting the 1” washer, placing the lap onto the rotation table, then placing the 1 ½” washer in its center. Insert the bolt through the washers and flat lap and tighten them to the rotation table.

WATER DRAIN

The LapMaster’s water drain is located on the bottom of the machine. This drain is not closable and should be piped to a separate reservoir for operation. Do not pour your wastewater slurry down the drain, as the sediment can harden within your pipes. Let the sediment settle to the bottom of your containers. You may pour out the container on a gravel area, or you may let the water evaporate and dispose of the sludge in the trash or a gravel area.

nodes.title: 18 in. SawMaster Manual
nodes.body:
Welcome to your new Rhino Lapidary 18” SawMaster!

  • Wheel Attachment, x2

  • Wheel Attachment w/ Stop, x2

  • Wheel Attachment Bolt, x4

  • Wheel Attachment Nut, x4

  • Wheel Attachment Washer, x4

  • Wrench, x2

INITIAL SETUP

Before using your machine, read ALL directions. You will need to install and calibrate a blade, fill with cutting oil, and calibrate the automatic feed choke before starting your first slabbing project.

Note: Please see the SAW BLADE MOUNT section below for blade mounting instructions.

Note: Any reference of “forward,” “front,” “backward,” or “back” in these instructions refers to the respective front or back of the machine, not the user’s perspective. The front of the machine is where the control box and power switch are located.

When using an 18” saw blade, fill the oil reservoir with 8 to 10 gallons of cutting oil. This ensures the blade sits in the liquid at about ½” to 2” in depth. This machine can also be operated with saw blades as small as 12”, but more oil will be required to ensure the blade sits submerged in the liquid.

Important: Rhino Lapidary recommends using mineral oil, because water can cause interior parts of the machine to rust. URock oil can also be used in the SawMaster. It is important that the ratio of URock oil and water is properly mixed to prevent any rusting of the machine.

Automatic Feed Choke Calibration:
Before starting your first slabbing project, the automatic feed should be calibrated. See the AUTOMATIC FEED CHOKE section.

ACCESSORIES

Wheel Attachments:
The SawMaster comes with four foot attachments that allow for the machine to be mounted on wheels. Two of these wheels have a lever locking mechanism to prevent the machine from moving unexpectedly.

Important: If you choose to attach the wheels, do not operate the machine without locking them in place first.

Wrenches:
The SawMaster comes with two wrenches that are used to hold the arbor in place and prevent it from rotating when tightening or loosening the arbor nut.

Hydraulic Lid Stand:
The SawMaster comes with a hydraulic stand that automatically supports the lid while open. Because of the hydraulics, attempting to open the machine quickly may prove to be difficult. The lid can be opened with ease by lifting slowly.

Rock Catcher:
There is a polypropylene plastic catching basket for the cut ends of the stones you are cutting to safely fall into. This is located on the right side of the interior of the machine.

GENERAL

The 18” SawMaster is 37” in width and 52” in depth, and weighs approximately 287lbs. The machine frame is made of 6mm-thick reinforced steel.

Electrical Requirements:
The 18” SawMaster’s ¾ Horsepower primary motor runs on 110 Volts. The SawMaster’s automatic feed motor is ¼ Horsepower. It is highly recommended to operate this motor on a minimum 20 amperage circuit.

Important: Do not run this machine on a circuit or voltage not recommended for this machine. Motor start-up can jump to 21-22 amperage but will then settle back to below 20 amps. Make sure the machine has its own circuit for best performance.

Arbor and Blade Mount:
The SawMaster comes with a 1” arbor for mounting the saw blade. Saw blade sizes ranging from 18” to 12” can be used with this machine.

Note: Blade not included.

Control Box:
The electrical control box is located on the front of the machine and includes 7 visible controls:

  1. The red cylindrical indicator light near the top of the control box turns on when power is supplied to the machine. 

  2. The green cylindrical indicator light near the top of the control box turns on when the machine is operating and the saw blade is spinning.

  3. The red and yellow emergency stop button is located in the center of the control box (see SAFETY FEATURES for description).

  4. The power switch turns the machine on, preparing it for operation.

  5. The green “RUN” button initiates machine operation, but only works while the lid of the machine is closed and the lid safety catch is engaged (see SAFETY FEATURES for description of safety catch). 

  6. The red “STOP” button removes power from the saw blade. The machine will automatically stop if the lid safety catch is disengaged (see SAFETY FEATURES for description of safety catch).

  7. The alarm buzzer is located between the two indicator lights (see SAFETY FEATURES for description).

SAFETY FEATURES

Emergency Stop Button:
This button halts machine operation when pressed. Once the emergency stop has been engaged, it needs to be disengaged before operation can resume, which is done by twisting the emergency stop button clockwise.

Safety Catch:
The lid safety catch is located on the front left corner of the machine. When the lid is closed, it creates pressure on the safety catch. The pressure is removed when the lid is lifted. If the lid is lifted while the machine is operating, the safety catch engages and ceases operation of the machine.

Alarm Buzzer:
The alarm buzzer will sound whenever the machine is left on for more than a minute while the lid is raised or the lid safety catch is not engaged. This will sound like small, high-pitched beeps that go off approximately every second. To stop the alarm, simply close the lid or turn off the machine.

SAW BLADE MOUNT

Note: The wrenches provided with the machine are used to hold onto the indented part of the arbor to prevent the arbor from rotating while tightening or loosening the arbor nut. 

The arbor inside of the machine comes with a washer spacer and a hex nut for securing a blade on the arbor. To attach a blade, remove the nut and washer, then slide your blade onto the arbor. The SawMaster arbor is meant for blades with a 1” diameter arbor hole. Secure your blade by sliding on the washer and nut, then tightening the nut. 

Aligning the Blade:
To check the alignment of the blade you must take two measurements:

  1. Adjust the sled to be situated next to the front edge of the blade. Measure the distance between the front of the blade to the nearest edge of the sled.

  2. Adjust the sled to be situated next to the back edge of the blade. Rotate the blade 180 degrees so the spot you just measured on the front edge is now the back edge. Measure the distance between the back of the blade to the nearest edge of the sled.

If these two measurements are the same, the saw is perfectly aligned. The automatic vice sled tracks are mounted using 4 U-bolts, which can be loosened to shift the sled into alignment, then tightened to secure the sled tracks once more. This avoids needing to remount the saw blade to align the machine before operation.

Important: Do not run the machine while the blade is not aligned. This may ruin the blade and lead to messy cuts.

AUTOMATIC VICE SLED

The automatic vice sled is attached to two sealed vertical bearings. While the machine is operating, this sled will move slowly towards the back of the machine.

Adjusting Forward/Backwards:
The sled can be manually adjusted forwards or backwards using a clamp mechanism on the front side of the sled. Pulling both levers outwards simultaneously disengages the clamping mechanism, while pushing both levers inwards simultaneously engages the clamping mechanism. Replacements for the clamping mechanism can be bought at RhinoLapidary.com.

Automatic Feed Maintenance:
There are two grease ports on either side of the automatic feed rod where it is mounted in the front and the back of the machine. 

Note: Rhino Lapidary recommends that, with regular or daily use, the automatic feed rod should be greased about once per month.

Adjusting Left/Right:
The sled can be manually adjusted left or right using the adjustment wheel located on the left side of the sled. Spinning this wheel towards the back of the machine moves the vice sled to the right, and spinning this gear towards the front of the machine moves the vice sled to the left. To secure the vice sled in place in this direction, tighten the black knob located on the side of the adjustment wheel.

There are numerical markers along this adjustment wheel that dictate the horizontal movement distance measured in millimeters. Rotating the adjustment wheel from one numerical marker to another makes for a 1mm horizontal adjustment.

Engaging the Vice:
To mount a stone for cutting, you must unscrew the wing nuts high enough to fit your stone between the two vice plates. Once you have lifted the top vice plate and fit your stone between the bottom and top vice plate, rescrew the wing nuts to clamp the vice shut, securing your stone in place. Replacement sets for the vice plates can be bought at RhinoLapidary.com.

Important: When tightening the wing nuts, ensure the wings end up parallel to the saw blade. DO NOT run the machine while the wing nuts are not parallel to the saw blade. Rhino Lapidary recommends tightening and securing the back wing nut first, adjusting to a parallel position, then tightening and securing the front wing nut in a parallel position.

AUTOMATIC FEED STOPPER RODS

The SawMaster comes with two different lengths of automatic stopper rods. One of these can be mounted in the back left interior part of the machine. The length of these rods are not adjustable, so be sure to measure if your stone will be cut all the way through by the time the automatic feed sled connects with the automatic stopper. When the sled presses against the stopper rod, the machine will cease operation.

AUTOMATIC FEED CHOKE

The automatic feed motor is located on the back of the machine. A choke is attached to this motor, which can be tightened and loosened. The choke prevents machine strain if the cutting speed of the saw on a particular stone does not correlate with the feed motor speed. This must be calibrated before any stones are cut with this machine. 

Automatic Feed Choke Calibration:
Note: During operation, the tightened choke will rotate in tandem with the automatic feed motor.

To calibrate, first loosen the choke until it no longer rotates while the automatic feed motor is running. The ideal tightness of the choke is tight enough to rotate a full rotation without stuttering, but loose enough to stop spinning if any resistance is applied by a rock during a cut. To achieve this, slowly tighten the choke while the machine is operating with no rock in the vice. You will start to notice the choke rotate with the rotation of the feed motor; observe the rotation before tightening further.

If the choke completes a full rotation without buffering, stuttering, or otherwise briefly halting, the choke is at an ideal tightness. Otherwise, repeat the above step (tighten and observe), until the choke reaches an ideal tightness.

Important: Do not use this machine to cut while the choke has not been calibrated. This will damage the blade, motor, and belt as it overstrains the system.

MOTOR BELT AND GUARD

The motor belt is located on the right side of the machine, and is encased in a grey metal guard. This machine uses a XX” belt. 

Replacing the Belt:
While the machine is off, unscrew the two bolts located on the side of the metal guard, and then remove the guard to access the belt tracks. Remove the old rubber belt and replace with a new one, ensuring it is placed evenly on the rotating tracks. Reposition the belt guard and secure with the two screws before turning the machine on.

nodes.title: 36 in. SawMaster Manual
nodes.body:
Welcome to your new Rhino Lapidary 36” SawMaster!

  • Wheel Attachment, x2

  • Wheel Attachment w/ Stop, x2

  • Wheel Attachment Bolt, x4

The SawMaster comes with two wrenches that are used to hold the arbor in place and prevent it from rotating when tightening or loosening the arbor nut.

Hydraulic Lid Stand:
The SawMaster comes with a hydraulic stand that automatically supports the lid while open. Because of the hydraulics, attempting to open the machine quickly may prove to be difficult. The lid can be opened with ease by lifting slowly.

Rock Catcher:
There is a polypropylene plastic catching basket for the cut ends of the stones you are cutting to safely fall into. This is located on the right side of the interior of the machine.

GENERAL

The 36” SawMaster is XX” in width and XX” in depth, and weighs approximately XXXlbs. The machine frame is made of 6mm-thick reinforced steel.

Electrical Requirements:
The 36” SawMaster’s 3 Horsepower primary motor runs on 110 Volts. The SawMaster’s automatic feed motor is ¼ Horsepower. It is highly recommended to operate this motor on a minimum 20 amperage circuit.

Important: Do not run this machine on a circuit or voltage not recommended for this machine. Motor start-up can jump to 21-22 amperage but will then settle back to below 20 amps. Make sure the machine has its own circuit for best performance.

Arbor and Blade Mount:
The SawMaster comes with a 1” arbor for mounting the saw blade.

Note: Blade not included.

Control Box:
The electrical control box is located on the front of the machine and includes 7 visible controls:

  1. The red cylindrical indicator light near the top of the control box turns on when power is supplied to the machine. 

  2. The green cylindrical indicator light near the top of the control box turns on when the machine is operating and the saw blade is spinning.

  3. The red and yellow emergency stop button is located in the center of the control box (see SAFETY FEATURES for description).

  4. The power switch turns the machine on, preparing it for operation.

  5. The green “RUN” button initiates machine operation, but only works while the lid of the machine is closed and the lid safety catch is engaged (see SAFETY FEATURES for description of safety catch). 

  6. The red “STOP” button removes power from the saw blade. The machine will automatically stop if the lid safety catch is disengaged (see SAFETY FEATURES for description of safety catch).

  7. The alarm buzzer is located between the two indicator lights (see SAFETY FEATURES for description).

SAFETY FEATURES

Emergency Stop Button:
This button halts machine operation when pressed. Once the emergency stop has been engaged, it needs to be disengaged before operation can resume, which is done by twisting the emergency stop button clockwise.

Safety Catch:
The lid safety catch is located on the front left corner of the machine. When the lid is closed, it creates pressure on the safety catch. The pressure is removed when the lid is lifted. If the lid is lifted while the machine is operating, the safety catch engages and ceases operation of the machine.

Alarm Buzzer:
The alarm buzzer will sound whenever the machine is left on for more than a minute while the lid is raised or the lid safety catch is not engaged. This will sound like small, high-pitched beeps that go off approximately every second. To stop the alarm, simply close the lid or turn off the machine.

SAW BLADE MOUNT

Note: The wrenches provided with the machine are used to hold onto the indented part of the arbor to prevent the arbor from rotating while tightening or loosening the arbor nut. 

The arbor inside of the machine comes with a washer spacer and a hex nut for securing a blade on the arbor. To attach a blade, remove the nut and washer, then slide your blade onto the arbor. The SawMaster arbor is meant for blades with a 1” diameter arbor hole. Secure your blade by sliding on the washer and nut, then tightening the nut. 

Aligning the Blade:
To check the alignment of the blade you must take two measurements:

  1. Adjust the sled to be situated next to the front edge of the blade. Measure the distance between the front of the blade to the nearest edge of the sled.

  2. Adjust the sled to be situated next to the back edge of the blade. Rotate the blade 180 degrees so the spot you just measured on the front edge is now the back edge. Measure the distance between the back of the blade to the nearest edge of the sled.

If these two measurements are the same, the saw is perfectly aligned. The automatic vice sled tracks are mounted using 4 U-bolts, which can be loosened to shift the sled into alignment, then tightened to secure the sled tracks once more. This avoids needing to remount the saw blade to align the machine before operation.

Important: Do not run the machine while the blade is not aligned. This may ruin the blade and lead to messy cuts.

AUTOMATIC VICE SLED

The automatic vice sled is attached to two sealed vertical bearings. While the machine is operating, this sled will move slowly towards the back of the machine.

Adjusting Forward/Backwards:
The sled can be manually adjusted forwards or backwards using a clamp mechanism on the front side of the sled. Pulling both levers outwards simultaneously disengages the clamping mechanism, while pushing both levers inwards simultaneously engages the clamping mechanism. Replacements for the clamping mechanism can be bought at RhinoLapidary.com.

Automatic Feed Maintenance:
There are two grease ports on either side of the automatic feed rod where it is mounted in the front and the back of the machine. 

Note: Rhino Lapidary recommends that, with regular or daily use, the automatic feed rod should be greased about once per month.

Adjusting Left/Right:
The sled can be manually adjusted left or right using the adjustment wheel located on the left side of the sled. Spinning this wheel towards the <back?> of the machine moves the vice sled to the right, and spinning this gear towards the <front?> of the machine moves the vice sled to the left. To secure the vice sled in place in this direction, tighten the black knob located on the side of the adjustment wheel.

There are numerical markers along this adjustment wheel that dictate the horizontal movement distance measured in millimeters. Rotating the adjustment wheel from one numerical marker to another makes for a 1mm horizontal adjustment.

Engaging the Vice:
To mount a stone for cutting, you must unscrew the wing nuts high enough to fit your stone between the two vice plates. Once you have lifted the top vice plate and fit your stone between the bottom and top vice plate, rescrew the wing nuts to clamp the vice shut, securing your stone in place. Replacement sets for the vice plates can be bought at RhinoLapidary.com.

Important: When tightening the wing nuts, ensure the wings end up parallel to the saw blade. DO NOT run the machine while the wing nuts are not parallel to the saw blade. Rhino Lapidary recommends tightening and securing the back wing nut first, adjusting to a parallel position, then tightening and securing the front wing nut in a parallel position.

AUTOMATIC FEED STOPPER RODS

The SawMaster comes with two different lengths of automatic stopper rods. One of these can be mounted in the back left interior part of the machine. The length of these rods are not adjustable, so be sure to measure if your stone will be cut all the way through by the time the automatic feed sled connects with the automatic stopper. When the sled presses against the stopper rod, the machine will cease operation.

AUTOMATIC FEED CHOKE

The automatic feed motor is located on the back of the machine. A choke is attached to this motor, which can be tightened and loosened. The choke prevents machine strain if the cutting speed of the saw on a particular stone does not correlate with the feed motor speed. This must be calibrated before any stones are cut with this machine. 

Automatic Feed Choke Calibration:
Note: During operation, the tightened choke will rotate in tandem with the automatic feed motor.

To calibrate, first loosen the choke until it no longer rotates while the automatic feed motor is running. The ideal tightness of the choke is tight enough to rotate a full rotation without stuttering, but loose enough to stop spinning if any resistance is applied by a rock during a cut. To achieve this, slowly tighten the choke while the machine is operating with no rock in the vice. You will start to notice the choke rotate with the rotation of the feed motor; observe the rotation before tightening further.

If the choke completes a full rotation without buffering, stuttering, or otherwise briefly halting, the choke is at an ideal tightness. Otherwise, repeat the above step (tighten and observe), until the choke reaches an ideal tightness.

Important: Do not use this machine to cut while the choke has not been calibrated. This will damage the blade, motor, and belt as it overstrains the system.

MOTOR BELT AND GUARD

The motor belt is located on the right side of the machine, and is encased in a grey metal guard. This machine uses a XX” belt. 

Replacing the Belt:
While the machine is off, unscrew the two bolts located on the side of the metal guard, and then remove the guard to access the belt tracks. Remove the old rubber belt and replace with a new one, ensuring it is placed evenly on the rotating tracks. Reposition the belt guard and secure with the two screws before turning the machine on.

nodes.title: TrimMaster Manual
nodes.body:
Welcome to your new Rhino Lapidary TrimMaster!

  • Plexiglass tabletop insert

  • 26” power grip belt

  • Belt cover

  • 2 pulleys

  • 2 triangular latch screws

  • 4 cylindrical plastic spacers

  • 4 lock nut fixtures (screw, washer, & nut)

  • Splash guard, upper

  • Splash guard, front

  • Straight edge guide

  • Arbor nut

  • ⅝” Arbor washers

  • ⅝” to 1” Arbor adapter washers

  • ⅝” to 1 ⅛” Arbor adapter washers

  • Drain plug

  • 4 adjustable feet

INITIAL SETUP

The tabletop TrimMaster can be placed on any flat, sturdy surface. You will need to install a blade and fill the lower reservoir with liquid before use. See SAW BLADE MOUNT for instructions on installing a blade.

The TrimMaster includes an easily accessible interior, held by 2 latches on either side of the machine. Unlatching each of these allows the top plate to be lifted, exposing the interior of the machine: including the arbor, bearings, and oil reservoir. When you are finished accessing the interior reservoir of the machine, carefully replace the top plate and secure the 2 latches.

Important: Do not turn on the machine while latches are unsecured, otherwise you may cause damage to the blade.

Fill the oil reservoir with your choice of liquid (either mineral oil or water) to ensure the blade sits in the liquid at ⅝” to 1” in depth. 

Important: Rhino Lapidary recommends using mineral oil, because water can cause interior parts of the machine to rust.

GENERAL

The TrimMaster is 15” in width and 25” in depth, and weighs approximately 67lbs. The machine frame is made of 6mm-thick reinforced steel.

Arbor and Blade Mount:
The TrimMaster has a ⅝” arbor for mounting a saw blade. Both 6” and 8” saw blades can be used with this machine, with either a ⅝”, 1”, or 1 ⅛” arbor hole.

Note: Blade not included.

Electrical Requirements:
The TrimMaster’s ¾ Horsepower motor runs on 110 Volts and it is highly recommended to operate this motor on a minimum 20 amperage circuit.

Important: Do not run this machine on a circuit or voltage not recommended for this machine. Motor start-up performance can jump to 21-22 amperage but will then settle back to below 20 amps. Make sure the machine has its own circuit for best performance.

Adjustable Feet:
Each of the TrimMaster’s four feet can be raised or lowered individually. 

Note: It is recommended to adjust the front of the machine slightly higher than the back of the machine. This allows accumulated oil spray to collect towards the draining holes in the plexiglass insert.

Adjustable Blade Guard:
The TrimMaster comes with an adjustable blade guard to reduce splash and increase blade lubrication. This may be lowered or raised to the desired angle.

SAW BLADE MOUNT

Note: You may need to hold onto the arbor or saw blade to prevent the arbor from rotating while tightening or loosening the arbor nut. 

The arbor inside of the machine comes with a washer spacer and a hex nut for securing the blade on the arbor. To attach a blade, remove the nut and washer, then slide your blade onto the arbor. The TrimMaster is meant for blades with a ⅝” diameter arbor hole. Saw blades with a 1” or 1 ⅛” arbor hole can be mounted using the arbor washer adapter sets. Secure your blade by sliding on the washer and nut, then tightening the nut. 

MOTOR BELT AND GUARD

The motor belt is located on the left side of the machine, and is encased in a grey metal guard. This machine uses a 26” belt. 

Replacing Belt:
While the machine is off, unscrew the three bolts located above, beneath, and in front of the metal guard and remove the guard to access the belt and pulleys. Then adjust the bolts securing the motor mount to the back of the machine. Pulling the motor towards the front of the machine provides slack to the motor belt, allowing it to be removed and replaced with a new one. Reposition the motor mount, ensuring that it is completely parallel with the back of the machine, then adjust the mounting bolts again. Reposition the belt guard and secure with the three screws before turning the machine back on.

Important: After any adjustments, always ensure the belt and the motor are mounted completely parallel with their respective steel walls. If the machine operates while the belt is not parallel, the belt may fly off or become damaged. If the machine operates while the motor is not parallel, the machine may sustain damage during operation.

TABLETOP INSERT

The tabletop insert with the blade slot is made of durable plexiglass. Replacements for this piece can be ordered through RhinoLapidary.com.

Raising the Insert:
Raising the plexiglass insert allows for cutting freeforms from large slabs at an even angle. Unscrew all four screws securing the plexiglass insert to the tabletop plate. Lift the plexiglass insert and place each of the four cylindrical plastic spacers inline with each of the screw locations. Replace the plexiglass insert atop of the placed spacers, then secure it again by screwing each of the screws back into the corners, making sure to screw through the center of the spacers as well.

MOUNTED GUIDE

The mounted guide provides a straight edge for cutting consistently. The guide can be adjusted left and right by loosening the twist knob on the brass bracket, moving the guide to the desired position, then tightening the same twist knob to secure it.

nodes.title: JadeMaster Manual
nodes.body:
Welcome to your new Rhino Lapidary JadeMaster!

  • <PARTS>

  • XX” Belt

  • Arbor nut

  • Arbor washer

INITIAL SETUP

Note: Please see the SAW BLADE MOUNT section below for blade mounting instructions.

Note: Any reference of “forward,” “front,” “backward,” or “back” in these instructions refers to the respective front or back of the machine, not the user’s perspective. The front of the machine is where the control box and power switch are located.

Fill the oil reservoir with 8 gallons of cutting oil. This ensures the blade sits in the liquid at about 2” in depth. 

Important: Rhino Lapidary recommends using mineral oil, because water can cause interior parts of the machine to rust. URock oil can also be used in the JadeMaster. It is important that the ratio of URock oil and water is properly mixed to prevent any rusting of the machine.

GENERAL

The JadeMaster is XX” in width and XX” in depth, and weighs approximately XXlbs. The machine frame is made of 6mm-thick reinforced steel.

Arbor and Blade Mount:
The JadeMaster comes with a 1” arbor for mounting the saw blade. 14” saw blades can be used with this machine.  A 12” blade can also be used in this machine, but would require the reservoir to be filled more to submerge the blade to 2” in depth.

Note: Blade not included.

Motor and Electrical Requirements:
The JadeMaster’s ¾ Horsepower motor runs on 110 Volts and it is highly recommended to operate this motor on a minimum 20 amperage circuit. This motor lets a 14” blade cut at 23 ½” per hour, or 10mm per minute.

Important: Do not run this machine on a circuit or voltage not recommended for this machine. Motor start-up can jump to 21-22 amperage but will then settle back to below 20 amps. Make sure the machine has its own circuit for best performance.

Control Box:
The electrical control box is located on the front of the machine and includes a horizontal switch on the right side. Pulling the switch forwards starts the machine, and pushing backwards stops it.

Adjustable Feet:
Each of the JadeMaster’s four feet can be raised or lowered individually with a wrench. 

Note: Rhino Lapidary recommends adjusting the JadeMaster to be exactly level. This keeps the blade consistently in oil and allows the vice sled to operate as expected.

SAW BLADE MOUNT

Note: You may need to hold onto the arbor or saw blade to prevent the arbor from rotating while tightening or loosening the arbor nut. 

The arbor inside of the machine comes with a washer spacer and a hex nut for securing the blade on the arbor. To attach a blade, remove the nut and washer, then slide your blade onto the arbor. The JadeMaster arbor is meant for blades with a 1” diameter arbor hole. Secure your blade by sliding on the washer and nut, then tightening the nut. 

Aligning the Blade:
To check the alignment of the blade you must take two measurements:

  1. Adjust the sled to be situated next to the front edge of the blade. Measure the distance between the front of the blade to the nearest edge of the sled.

  2. Adjust the sled to be situated next to the back edge of the blade. Rotate the blade 180 degrees so the spot you just measured on the front edge is now the back edge. Measure the distance between the back of the blade to the nearest edge of the sled.

If these two measurements are the same, the saw is perfectly aligned. Adjust the arbor washer and arbor nut until these two measurements are nearly the same.

Important: Do not run the machine while the blade is not aligned. This may ruin the blade and lead to messy cuts.

MOTOR BELT AND GUARD

The motor belt is located on the back left side of the machine, and is encased in a grey metal guard. This machine uses a XX” belt. 

Replacing Belt:
While the machine is off, unscrew the two bolts located on the side of the metal guard, and then remove the guard to access the belt tracks. Remove the old rubber belt and replace with a new one, ensuring it is placed evenly on the rotating tracks. Reposition the belt guard and secure with the two screws before turning the machine on.

AUTOMATIC VICE SLED

The automatic vice sled is attached to two sealed vertical bearings. While the machine is operating, this sled will move slowly towards the back of the machine.

Adjusting Forward/Backwards:
The sled can be manually adjusted forwards or backwards using a clamp release mechanism on the backside of the sled. Pulling the lever on the back of the sled to the right releases the clamp on the riveted rod, allowing the sled to slide forwards and backwards. Releasing the lever and letting it spring back to the left engages the rivet clamp and locks the sled in place.

Adjusting Left/Right:
The sled can be manually adjusted left or right using the thumb spindle located on the right side of the sled. Spinning this gear towards the back of the machine moves the vice sled to the right, and spinning this gear towards the front of the machine moves the vice sled to the left. To secure the vice sled in place in this direction, tighten the black knob located on the side of the thumb spindle.

Engaging the Vice:
To mount a stone for cutting, you must unscrew the wing nuts high enough to fit your stone between the two vice plates. Once you have lifted the top vice plate and fit your stone between the bottom and top vice plate, rescrew the wing nuts to clamp the vice shut, securing your stone in place.

Important: When tightening the wing nuts, ensure the wings end up parallel to the saw blade. DO NOT run the machine while the wing nuts are not parallel to the saw blade. Rhino Lapidary recommends tightening and securing the back wing nut first, adjusting to a parallel position, then tightening and securing the front wing nut in a parallel position.

VICE RISER

The JadeMaster has two cutting modes: Low Cut Position, which allows for a cutting height of 5 ½” and a cutting length of 5”, and a High Cut Position, which allows for a cutting height of 4 ½” and a cutting length of 13”. 

Important: Do not cut pieces larger than 5” while in Low Cut Position.

The vice riser can be attached to the automatic vice sled by first removing the wing nuts from the two large screws. Then remove the vice plates, and slide the riser through the large screws, resting on the sled. Tighten the fastening bolt on the right side of the riser to secure it to the sled. Then replace the vice plates, ensuring the riser fastening bolt fits through the space on the right side of the bottom vice plate. Replace the wing nuts onto the screws.

Important: When tightening the wing nuts, ensure the wings end up parallel to the saw blade. DO NOT run the machine while the wing nuts are not parallel to the saw blade. Rhino Lapidary recommends tightening and securing the back wing nut first, adjusting to a parallel position, then tightening and securing the front wing nut in a parallel position.

PURPLE JADE BEAD STOPPER

The automatic stopping mechanism on the JadeMaster consists of a string of Purple Jade beads strung between the automatic vice sled and the machine’s power switch. The desired distance of a cut can be dictated by how the bead string is attached to the sled. There is a thin vertical metal slot located on the front right side of the sled, where the bead strand can be inserted. The number of beads kept on either side of the slot determines the length of the cut. Once the bead string is pulled taut, the power switch will automatically be switched off.

nodes.title: BeadMaster Manual
nodes.body:
Welcome to your new Rhino Lapidary BeadMaster!

  • Arbor nut

  • Arbor washer

INITIAL SETUP

Control Box Mount:
When you first receive your Rhino Lapidary BeadMaster, the control box needs to be mounted onto the machine frame. On the bottom of the control box, there is a metal plate with two holes for screws. This is to be mounted on the top left frontside of the machine’s back plate. This can be done using the two screws and nuts the machine back plate comes attached with.

Water Feed:
The grinding wheel arbor and motor belt are mounted on the left side of the BeadMaster. On the top of this area, there is a spout where a continuous water source can be attached using rubber tubing and a gasket. The blue valve attached to this spout controls the flow of the water source onto the grinding wheel.

Drain and Adjustable Feet:
The BeadMaster comes with adjustable feet which allows users to control the incline of the baseplate. There is a drain in the back right corner of the baseplate, which empties out from the lower back right side of the machine frame. This drain should be attached to rubber tubing using a gasket and trailed to a reservoir for the excess water. To ensure collected water from machine usage is draining properly, adjust the front and left feet slightly higher than the back right foot. 

GENERAL

The BeadMaster is 18 ⅜” in width and 27” in depth, and weighs approximately 90lbs. The machine frame is made of 6mm-thick reinforced steel.

Control Box:
The grey control box is located on the back left part of the BeadMaster. The control box includes an indicator light, emergency stop button, and power switch. The green power switch turns the machine on when flipped clockwise, or off when flipped counterclockwise. The red indicator light will turn on when the machine is supplied with power. The red and yellow emergency stop button, when pressed, stops any machine operation. To disengage the emergency stop button, twist the button clockwise. 

Electrical Requirements:
The BeadMaster’s ¾ Horsepower motor runs on 110 Volts and it is highly recommended to operate this motor on a minimum 20 amperage circuit.

Important: Do not run this machine on a circuit or voltage not recommended for this machine. Motor start-up can jump to 21-22 amperage but will then settle back to below 20 amps. Make sure the machine has its own circuit for best performance.

Arbor and Wheel Mount:
The BeadMaster comes with a 1” arbor for mounting the grinding wheel. 6” grinding wheels can be used with this machine. 

Note: Grinding wheel not included.

GRINDING WHEEL MOUNT

Note: You may need to secure the arbor rotationally while tightening or loosening the arbor nut. This can be done by inserting an Allen wrench into the space on its end.

The arbor is located on the left of the machine and comes with a washer spacer and a hex nut for securing a wheel onto the arbor. To attach a grinding wheel, the side plate of the black wheel cover must be removed.  Remove the screws that are securing the side plate, then remove the nut and washer. Slide the wheel onto the arbor, replace the washer and nut, and then tighten the nut to secure the wheel.. Afterwards, reattach the black sideplate, replacing each of the screws back in their positions.

Note: The BeadMaster arbor is meant for wheels with a 1” diameter arbor hole. The wheel space accommodates wheels with a width ranging from 5mm to 12mm.

MOTOR BELT AND GUARD

The motor belt is located on the back left side of the machine, and is encased in a grey metal guard. This machine uses a XX” belt. 

Replacing Belt:
While the machine is off, unscrew the two bolts located on the side of the metal guard, and then remove the guard to access the belt tracks. Remove the old rubber belt and replace with a new one, ensuring it is placed evenly on the rotating tracks. Reposition the belt guard and secure with the two screws before turning the machine on.

PREFORM BUGGY

Note: Lifting the buggy into the upright position engages the motor while the machine is switched on.

The preform buggy is located in the front of the machine, and consists of two important parts: the yellow plastic stage and the black pull handle. 

The yellow plastic stage is where prepared cubic stone preforms can be placed to be ground into a bead shape. Creating cubic preforms can be done using Rhino Lapidary’s TrimMaster. When the buggy is set into the upright position while the stage holds a preform, the BeadMaster will automatically grind and rotate the preform using the grinding wheel and the buggy’s rubber rotation wheel in tandem.

The black pull handle is the only other part of the buggy that needs to be interacted with to operate the machine. This is what is used to switch the buggy between upright position (pushing towards the back of the machine so the stage is upright) and the resting position (pulling towards the front of the machine so the stage is angled). The buggy’s rotation wheel and the grinding wheel will not start until the buggy is in the upright position.

Important: Pull the buggy into the resting position before turning on the BeadMaster. Once you have secured your preform, you can then slowly lift the buggy into the upright position.

nodes.title: ShapeMaster Manual
nodes.body:
Welcome to your new Rhino Lapidary ShapeMaster!

  • Wedge Heads, medium

  • Wedge Heads, small

  • Handcrank Handle, x2

  • Shape Template, x29

INITIAL SETUP

Control Box Mount:
When you first receive your Rhino Lapidary ShapeMaster, the control box needs to be mounted onto the machine frame. On the bottom of the control box, there is a metal plate with two holes for screws. This is to be mounted on the top left frontside of the machine’s back plate. This can be done using the two screws and nuts the machine back plate comes attached with.

Material Carriage Adjustment:
When you first receive your Rhino Lapidary ShapeMaster, the material carriage will be adjusted away from the grinding wheel to fit the machine in its box. See the MATERIAL CARRIAGE section for instructions on how to adjust the carriage horizontally.

Water Feed:
The grinding wheel arbor and motor belt are mounted on the left side of the BeadMaster. On the top of this area, there is a spout where a continuous water source can be attached using rubber tubing and a gasket. The blue valve attached to this spout controls the flow of the water source through the white hose that sprays onto the felt pad above the grinding wheel.

Drain and Adjustable Feet:
The ShapeMaster comes with adjustable feet which allows users to control the incline of the baseplate. There is a drain in the back right corner of the baseplate, which empties out from the lower back right side of the machine frame. This drain should be attached to rubber tubing using a gasket and trailed to a reservoir for the excess water. 

Important: To ensure collected water from machine usage is draining properly, Rhino Lapidary suggests adjusting the front and left feet slightly higher than the back right foot. 

GENERAL

The ShapeMaster is 18 ¾” in width and 27” in depth, and weighs approximately 115lbs. The machine frame is made of 6mm-thick reinforced steel.

Electrical Requirements:
The ShapeMaster’s ¾ Horsepower motor runs on 110 Volts and it is highly recommended to operate this motor on a minimum 20 amperage circuit.

Important: Do not run this machine on a circuit or voltage not recommended for this machine. Motor start-up can jump to 21-22 amperage but will then settle back to below 20 amps. Make sure the machine has its own circuit for best performance.

Control Box:
The grey control box is located on the back left part of the ShapeMaster. The control box includes an indicator light, emergency stop button, and power switch. The red indicator light will turn on when the machine is supplied with power. The red and yellow emergency stop button, when pressed, stops any machine operation. To disengage the emergency stop button, twist the button clockwise. The green power switch turns the machine on when flipped clockwise, or off when flipped counterclockwise.

Arbor and Wheel Mount:
The ShapeMaster comes with a 1” arbor for mounting the grinding wheel. 6” grinding wheels can be used with this machine. 

Note: Grinding wheel not included.

GRINDING WHEEL MOUNT

Note: You may need to secure the arbor rotationally while tightening or loosening the arbor nut. This can be done by inserting an Allen wrench into the space on its end.

The arbor, located on the left of the machine, comes with a washer spacer and a hex nut for securing the wheel onto the arbor. To access this area, you must first adjust the TEMPLATE CHASSIS to give you space to operate in the arbor area, which can be done after loosening the chassis knob. To attach or replace a grinding wheel, remove the screws securing the black side plate from which the end of the arbor protrudes. Remove the side plate, then remove the nut and washer. Now the wheel can slide onto the arbor and secure it by sliding on the washer and nut, then tightening the nut. Afterwards, reattach the black sideplate, replacing each of the screws back in their positions.

Note: The ShapeMaster arbor is meant for wheels with a 1” diameter arbor hole. The wheel space accommodates wheels with a width ranging from Xmm to XXmm.

TEMPLATE MOUNT

The template mount is located on the right side of the machine. There is a left-handed hand crank on its side that loosens when turning clockwise, and tightens when turning counterclockwise. When the hand crank is loosened and removed, you can insert or replace one of the 29 shape templates that come with the machine, which mounts onto the spoke between the hand crank and the support post.

TEMPLATE CHASSIS

The template chassis is also located on the right side of the machine, but is closer to the back, behind the template mount. This device is used to guide the machine against the shape template and give your stone the desired shape. The chassis can be adjusted forwards and backwards, which determines the amount that will be ground off of your mounted stone to create the desired shape: the further towards the back of the machine the chassis is, the more material will be ground off of your stone before the chassis makes contact with the shape template guide.

MATERIAL CARRIAGE

Note: There are two places to tighten the material carriage support posts: on the top and on the bottom. Adjust both the top and bottom when preparing material to be shaped by this machine.

The material carriage is located at the front of the machine, on a track in front of the grinding wheel. This is where the wedge heads that come with the machine are used to hold material in the clamp during operation.

Horizontal Adjustment:
There are two bolts that press against the base plate of the material carriage; on the left side of the carriage, there is one on a bracket in the front and one on a bracket in the back. These need to be loosened in order to adjust the carriage’s placement horizontally.

Mounting Material:
After loosening the top of the material clamp by turning the left-side hand crank, you can place wedge heads on either side of the inner spokes, using an allen wrench to tighten and secure the heads. Once the heads are attached, your material can be placed between the two heads and the top of the material clamp posts can be tightened to secure the material in place.

Vertical Alignment:
The two metal support posts that flank the material clamp have two points of tightening and loosening: the upper part, which is adjusted using the left-side hand crank, and the lower part, which is connected on a threaded bar with two hex nuts. Vertical alignment can be achieved by first clamping the material securely on the top, then moving the hex nuts to shift the bases of the support posts to become vertically parallel.

Important: Align the two material carriage support posts before operating this machine. They should be vertically parallel with each other before shaping any material.

nodes.title: EM-1 Manual
nodes.body:
Welcome to your new Rhino Lapidary EM-1!

1 motor, attached to black tabletop stand 

  • Stand includes water filtration system and 2 storage drawers

1 magnifying lens

1 industrial worklamp

1 arbor shaft for trim saw attachment

  • with metal spacer and brass nut

1 trim saw blade

1 flat lap

2 magnetic flat lap discs

  • 6” felt polishing pad

  • 6” disc 80 grit

2 wrist rests

1 water pump

2 brass spray nozzles

2 tubes for spray nozzles

1 spoke wrench

1 hex key (Allen wrench)

1 crescent wrench

2 blue plexiglass bottom trays (left & right)

1 blue plexiglass top shield (for right side only)

2 blue moss filtration pads (left & right)

1 flex shaft attachment

  • with 18pc accessory set and 3pc attachment heads

  • Flexible Shaft bit turntable

2 arbor sleeves (left & right)

  • with yellow spacers and brass nut

6 arbor wheels:

  • 6” Bonded Diamond Wheel 60 grit

  • 6” Bonded Diamond Wheel 220 grit

  • 6” Resin Bond Diamond Wheel 280 grit

  • 6” Resin Bond Diamond Wheel 600 grit

  • 6” Resin Bond Diamond Wheel 1200 grit

  • 6” Resin Bond Diamond Wheel 3000 grit

DIALUX Superfinishing paste

DIALUX Polishing paste

1 left Metal Spindle

1 right Metal Spindle

4 metalsmithing wheels:

  • 6” soft buffing wheel

  • 6” hard buffing wheel

  • 4” sanding wheel

  • 3” polishing brush wheel

INITIAL SETUP

Lift the motor out of the box by holding onto both arbor handles and lifting straight up. Place on a sturdy surface. 

The machine motor will need to be loosened from the base to assemble the plexiglass sides. Using a wrench and hex key, hold the nut from underneath using the wrench and loosen the 4 bolts on top. 

Match up the correct blue plexiglass pieces for each side of the machine. With the plexiglass sides in place, retighten the nuts underneath the machine and secure the arbor to the base. Place the matching blue moss pad into each plexiglass side.

ACCESSORIES

The lamp arm sits in the large hole on the top of the back section of the machine and slides in. Two small wires from the back of the machine connect to the lamp for power. 

The clamp on the magnifying lens is not needed and can be removed. Screw the magnifying lens arm into the head. The magnifying lens will sit in the other hole on the top of the back section of the machine and screw in. 

Three AAA Batteries (not included) are required to use the lamp function on the magnifying lens. Insert batteries as shown on magnifying lens.

Important: Do not plug in the machine until the lamp wires have been connected.

GENERAL

Arbor Arms:
There is an arbor arm sleeve, nut, and screw for the left side of the machine, and an arbor arm sleeve, nut, and screw for the right side of the machine. The left side nut and screw will tighten by turning them to the left. The right-side nut and screw will tighten by turning them to the right. 

Machine Controls:
The green switch controls on/off power. The dial on the right controls motor speed. The silver toggle has two positions. The “down” position is to be used for motor speeds 0-3,000rpm. When the toggle switch is moved to the “up” position, it can be used from motor speeds 0-5,000rpm. The “up” position of the toggle switch should only be used with the flex shaft. 

Important: The flex shaft should be the ONLY thing on the arbor when entering speeds over 3,000rpm. Remove all wheels and saw blade first before moving to higher speeds.

WATER RESERVOIR AND PUMP

Fill the red water reservoir with 3.5 gallons of water. Fill from the left side of the tank, indicated with “Fill the Tank Here.” 

Place the water pump on the right side, into the marked compartment of the red water tank. Secure the suction cups to the floor of the tank. Connect the power cord of the water pump to the corresponding cord at the back of the machine.

Important: The water pump turns on with the machine, and will continue to pump and filter water even when it is shut off of the wheels up top. Make sure the water reservoir is filled with water, or unplug the water pump when not in use so as to maintain water pump quality. Failure to do this will result in a water pump motor burn out!

TRIM SAW, right side ONLY

Important: Assemble off of the machine first.

Slide the saw blade onto its arbor sleeve. Slide the metal washer onto the arbor sleeve. Screw the metal nut in place to secure it. This makes the trim saw unit. 

Remove the metal spoke nut from the right arbor arm. Place the removable plexiglass protector over the arbor arm, directly against the side of the machine. When placing the metal spoke nut back into place, you can adjust the forward and backward tilt of the plexiglass into desired position. Using the metal spoke key, screw the metal spoke nut back on to secure. 

Slide the trim saw unit onto the arbor arm. Take the right arbor set screw and spring and slide it through the arborsleeve to screw in. Use the hex screw and apply pressure to screw the set screw until tightened. 

Place the water guard against the inside front of the blue plexiglass. Slide the black knob through the hole in the outside front of the blue plexiglass, and through the slot in the water guard. Slide the trim saw yellow spacer onto the black knob screw. Position the saw table onto the black knob screw, ensuring it does not touch either side of the saw blade or the arbor. Hand tighten the black knob. 

Place the brass spray nozzle into the plexiglass slot, positioned above the trim saw. 

Trim Saw Removal:
Unscrew the black knob to remove the saw table, spacer, and water guard. Unscrew the righthand arbor screw using a hex key and remove. To assist in pulling the trim saw unit off the arbor arm, loosen the metal spoke nut. Pull the trim saw unit off the arbor arm.

FLEX SHAFT, right side ONLY

Start with a bare arbor. Remove all previously placed pieces including the blue plexiglass shield. Screw the arborsize conversion bolt to the arbor arm. Screw the flexible shaft attachment onto the arbor arm. Clip the black tip of the flex shaft hose to the flexible shaft attachment. Slide the black cover up the flex shaft hose and screw onto the flexible shaft attachment. The hose should not be loose. 

There are three sizes of drill bit holders included. To change drill bits, insert and push the pin into the side of the flex shaft head. With the pin inserted, unscrew and remove the black piece. Insert desired drill bit holder and drill bit into the flex shaft head. Screw the black piece back on over the holder and bit to secure. Remove the pin, and ensure the bit is securely held in place.

Flex Shaft Removal:
Unscrew the black cover and pull the clip off the flexible shaft attachment. Unscrew the flexible shaft attachment and the arbor size conversion bolt.

GRINDING AND POLISHING WHEELS

Important: Assemble off of the machine first.

The left arbor sleeve, nut, and yellow spacers come packaged together in the box. The right arbor sleeve, nut, and yellow spacers come packaged together in the box. All of the diamond wheels are in box 2. 

On the left arbor sleeve, slide the wheels and spacers on in this order:

  1. 280 Grit Resin Wheel (black)

  2. Yellow spacer

  3. 220grit diamond wheel

  4. Yellow spacer

  5. 80 grit diamond wheel

  6. Yellow spacer-small

  7. Nut

On the right arbor sleeve, slide the wheels and spacers on in this order:

  1. 600 grit resin wheel (brown)

  2. Yellow spacer

  3. 1200 grit resin wheel (gray)

  4. Yellow spacer

  5. 3000 grit resin wheel (red)

  6. Yellow spacer-small

  7. Nut, or Flat Lap

Remove everything from the arbor arms except the metal spoke nut which is holding the blue plexiglass shields in place. Ensure the wheel units (left and right) are secure before placing onto the arbor arm. 

Slide the left arbor sleeve and wheel unit onto the left arbor arm. Insert the left arbor set screw and spring into the arbor sleeve, and tighten with the hex key. 

Slide the right arbor sleeve and wheel unit onto the right arbor arm. Insert the right arbor set screw and spring into the arbor sleeve, and tighten with the hex key. 

Align the arm rest with the holes on the sides of the blue plexiglass. Screw in a black knob on each side to secure. Repeat on the other side. Adjust forward and back to desired angle.

Important: Only move to higher speeds with the flex shaft. Do not move past polishing speeds with the grinding and polishing wheels on. Turn the dial SLOWLY to the left to decrease speed.

FLAT LAP

Follow all instructions for assembling the Grinding and Polishing wheels. Remove the nut and final yellow spacer from the right arbor sleeve. Screw on the flat lap. Attach desired magnetic grit or polish disc. Make sure lap and magnetic attachments are centered onto the flat lap wheel. Not having this centered can cause movement and play in arbor.

SILVERSMITHING WHEELS

Remove everything from the left arbor arm except the left metal spoke nut that holds the blue shield in place. The right metal spoke nut and plexiglass protector are optional for use with the silversmithing wheels. 

Select desired silversmithing wheels and tightly twist onto either metal spindle. Firmly push the left metal spindle onto the left arbor arm. Firmly push the right metal spindle onto the right arbor arm.

Important: Only move to higher speeds with the flex shaft. Do not move past 3,000rpm with the silversmithing wheels on. Turn the dial SLOWLY to the left to decrease speed.
